items.stem: The Hangul syllable 한 is read as:

options.rationale: Correct: ㅎ(h) + ㅏ(a) + ㄴ(n) combine to 'han'.
The initial consonant is ㅎ (h), so it is not 'nah'.
The final ㄴ adds an 'n' sound, giving 'han', not 'ha'.
The final consonant is ㄴ (n), not ㅇ (ng).

items.explanation: Correct: ㅎ(h) + ㅏ(a) + ㄴ(n) combine to 'han'.

items.stem: Choose the correct subject particle: '학생___ 공부해요.' (The student studies.)

options.rationale: Correct: 이 is the subject particle after a consonant-final noun like 학생.
가 is the subject particle after a vowel-final noun, not a consonant-final one.
를 marks an object, not a subject.
에 marks place or time, not the subject.
